rate_limit_policy.published: GitLab.com documents, per IP: unauthenticated traffic 500 requests/minute; GET /api/v4/groups/:id/projects 600 requests/minute. A proposed per-plan limit of 60 unauthenticated requests/hour is listed as not yet in effect.
rate_limit_policy.notes: The Groups and Projects APIs do not send RateLimit-* headers, so pacing relies on min_interval_seconds and max_requests (40 per run, below the proposed 60/hour). HTTP 429 Retry-After is honoured (afid.download.HttpClient).

robots.finding: 'User-Agent: *' with 'Disallow: /api/v*' (GitLab's stock template). The API is GitLab's documented programmatic interface, but whether this directive applies to bounded API clients needs a human decision before enabling.

review.access_mechanism: Unauthenticated GitLab REST v4 GET requests: group project listing and per-project branch listing. Verified working 2026-10-18 (docs/SOURCE_INTEGRATION.md).
review.legal_terms: Not reviewed: GitLab.com terms of use and the group's own terms (none found in the group description) must be reviewed for automated metadata listing.
review.endpoint_stability: Community-maintained group; GitLab REST v4 is versioned, but project layout and branch naming are conventions of the dump tooling, not a contract.
review.resource_consumption: At most max_requests (40) small JSON GETs per run, 2 s apart; no file contents, no clones, no archives.

providers.attribution: Firmware dumps published by the Android-Dumps community on GitLab.com (https://gitlab.com/Android-Dumps).
providers.license_notes: Dumps contain vendor firmware files under proprietary OEM terms. AFID records listing metadata only; no redistribution right is implied.

confirmed: Public group listing via GET /api/v4/groups/13303221/projects without authentication (2026-10-18).
One project per device and one branch per firmware build; branch names follow the Android build description '<product>-<type>-<release>-<build id>-<incremental>-<tags>' (snapshot 2026-10-19).
assumed: Namespace equals manufacturer and project name equals device codename: hints only, recorded as inferred.
Branch names stay build descriptions; a branch that does not parse yields null version fields.

providers.limitations: Lists git branches of extracted dumps, not downloadable firmware packages: file_name, file_size_bytes, sha256 and download_url stay null. soc, region and release_date are not available from the listing.

rate_limit_policy.notes: No published rate limit was found and the server sends no RateLimit-* headers (docs/SOURCE_INTEGRATION.md). Self-hosted on unknown capacity: paced at 3 s and 40 requests per run.

robots.finding: 'User-Agent: *' with 'Disallow: /api/v*' (GitLab's stock template, unchanged by the operator of the host). Needs a human decision before enabling; contacting the host's operator is the safest route.

rate_limit_policy.notes: Not a metadata source: the pipeline never contacts it.

review.access_mechanism: A shell tool that extracts firmware a user already has. AFID runs it only offline in the afid-firmware-worker image at pinned commit 303f5bba (config/settings.yml, docs/DUMPRX_INTEGRATION.md).
review.legal_terms: GPL-3.0-only; its bundled helper binaries have unresolved licences (docs/DUMPRX_INTEGRATION.md).
review.resource_consumption: Extraction needs several GiB of disk and minutes to hours per firmware; it is a separate workload with its own CPU, memory, timeout, storage and cost evaluation, not part of this pipeline.

providers.license_notes: Tool, not data. Its output inherits the firmware's proprietary terms.

confirmed: Offline extraction of a synthetic firmware ZIP in afid-firmware-worker (docs/DUMPRX_INTEGRATION.md).
assumed: Real vendor firmware extraction: not verified.
